minutes.headline: Cemetery Commission tabled the DPW's refund and Rainmaker password disputes; the chair says only commission votes can approve refunds.
minutes.summary: The commission interviewed a volunteer candidate, approved prior minutes, and heard two residents in public comment. The chair read a DPW director update, objected that three burial-lot refunds were issued without commission votes, and tabled the refund and Rainmaker software issues to April. Nothing else was formally decided.

attendees.role: member (speaks from the commission side, per his own point-of-order remark)

public_comment.topic: Opposed spending on Rainmaker data entry and headstone repair; argued burial-lot sales proceeds should reimburse the town under state law, called for a formal RFP before any cemetery work, and alleged bid violations at the North Cemetery parking lot.
Objected to how the DPW director was questioned at earlier meetings, called it a power play, and asked for an April agenda slot to speak longer than three minutes.
A speaker commented on the Rainmaker password during commission deliberation; the chair reminded that public comment was already used and a member raised a point of order about visitor interruption.

budget_items.what_was_said: A resident said entering historical records is cost prohibitive and cited a higher-tier Rainmaker option. The chair later said the commission bought it in 2010, upgraded in 2019, and pays annual license and maintenance fees.
A resident objected to a town manager-recommended capital plan request for headstone repair, arguing the town should only repair stones it controls.

budget_items.topic: Cemetery commission funds and reimbursement of town
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident said the commission holds funds and has not reimbursed the town for cemetery costs from lot sales.
The DPW director's note described refunds of burial rights, with perpetual care refunded in one case and not in two others. The chair said these refunds required commission votes.

decisions.decision: The chair will schedule Dave Rogers to speak at a future meeting, probably April, and asked him to submit his topic.
The Rainmaker password access issue was tabled; the commission may take it to the town manager and select board.
The burial lot refund issue was tabled to the next meeting; the chair said a pending March refund request was stopped until the commission votes.
A discussion with Richard McGrath was set for the April meeting, tentatively April 18.
A request for a 4-foot bench in the North Cemetery will be reviewed with the DPW and the requesting resident.

what_happened.line: The commission tabled the burial-lot refund issue to April after the chair objected that three refunds were issued without commission votes.
The chair said a pending March refund request was stopped until the commission votes on it.
The Rainmaker cemetery-records software password access issue was tabled; the commission may take it to the town manager and select board.
The commission approved the February 22 minutes and interviewed a candidate willing to run in the 2024 election.
Two residents spoke in public comment, one on Rainmaker data entry, headstone repair and lot-sale proceeds, the other asking for an April slot.

why_it_matters: Cemetery lot refunds and the records software are paid from cemetery funds and town money, so who has authority to approve a refund decides how those funds are handled.
Both issues were tabled with no vote, so nothing about the refunds or the software access is settled yet.
